# pangolin_resource_mtls (Resource)

Requires clients of a resource to present a certificate signed by a trusted CA. Certificates and the on/off switch live together here because Pangolin won't enable mTLS on a resource with no CA. The resource must have SSL enabled and can't be tcp or udp. A resource uses its shared resource policy's mTLS settings if the policy enables mTLS. Requires Pangolin 1.25 or later. Import using the resource ID, e.g. `terraform import pangolin_resource_mtls.example 5`; the API doesn't return PEM data, so the first apply after import uploads `ca_certificate_pem` and removes any other CA.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "pangolin_resource_mtls" "example" {
  resource_id        = pangolin_resource.example.resource_id
  ca_certificate_pem = file("${path.module}/client-ca.pem")
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `ca_certificate_pem` (String) Trusted CA certificates in PEM format. Holds one certificate or a bundle of up to 20; Pangolin stores each separately. This is the complete list: other CAs on the resource are removed.
- `resource_id` (Number) ID of the resource to protect.

### Optional

- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether clients must present a certificate. Defaults to true.

### Read-Only

- `fingerprints` (Set of String) SHA-256 fingerprints of the CA certificates on the resource.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import pangolin_resource_mtls.example 5
```
